common.patient_context: These patient services explain carboplatin monotherapy for metastatic breast cancer. The clinician protocol retains its separate gynaecology and, for q21, head-and-neck indications; breast trial outcomes must not populate those other cancer contexts.

mechanism.plain: Carboplatin is a platinum chemotherapy. It damages the DNA inside cancer cells, making it harder for them to divide and survive. It can also affect healthy cells, including blood-forming cells.

benefit_goal.plain: For breast cancer that has spread, treatment aims to shrink or control the cancer and relieve symptoms. Benefit and tolerability are reviewed regularly; it is not a promise of cure.
benefit_goal.source: NCCP breast indication p1; TNT advanced-disease population

dose_explanation.plain: The team chooses the treatment strength and calculates the amount from kidney function. Your dose may change after blood results or side effects. A lower dose or a delay can be part of the plan.
dose_explanation.clinician: The source range is AUC4–6, chosen by the Consultant; do not default everyone to AUC5 or AUC6, nor re-escalate a previously reduced prescription. Calvert outputs mg, not mg/m². GFR used is capped at125mL/min.

supportive_care.risk: HIGH at AUC≥4; MODERATE below4 per current NCCP V6 Table7, physical p12. Both requested standard source regimens are AUC4–6 and map to HIGH.
supportive_care.not_minimal: 00261 baseline had an unsafe minimal-risk mapping; corrected to high.
supportive_care.patient: Take the prescribed anti-sickness medicines before treatment and on the following days, even if you feel well. Follow your own prescription and contact the team if nausea or vomiting is not controlled.

following_days.days: Subsequent days: source does not specify end day
following_days.note: Printed row lacks PRN qualifier. Do not convert into an indefinite prescription; clinician/pharmacist must specify duration, appropriateness and any modifications.

qualifiers: NCIS Table1 allows clinician-selected ondansetron splitting to8mg twice daily or reduction to8mg once daily according to the individual patient.
Review ondansetron QT risk and other QT-prolonging medicines/electrolytes.
Check dexamethasone interactions, diabetes, sleep and infection effects; aprepitant/steroid interaction is already reflected in the specified row.
Review metoclopramide renal function, neurological contraindications, duration and extrapyramidal risk; do not automatically stack with olanzapine.
AUC reduction below4 requires an individual prophylaxis review; history of emesis and patient factors may justify continuing stronger protection.
No universal G-CSF, antibiotic, antiviral or acid-suppression prescription is stated by the carboplatin protocol. G-CSF requires individual febrile-neutropenia risk review.
Routine hypersensitivity premedication is usually unnecessary, but antiemetic prophylaxis is still required. Prior allergy/desensitisation is a separate specialist plan.

baseline: Blood count and kidney/liver blood tests.
Measured isotope GFR preferred; if unavailable use a verified appropriate estimated method.
Review prior platinum, allergies, hearing/nerve symptoms, prior dose reductions, other medicines and pregnancy/fertility issues.
before_each_cycle: Review symptoms, blood count, renal and liver profile.
Confirm current prescribed AUC, renal method and prior dose history.
For Cockcroft–Gault or Wright, creatinine must be obtained within48hours of treatment and dose recalculated as required.
For carrying forward an isotope-GFR dose, compare actual current creatinine with the value at measurement; >110% needs renal reassessment consideration.
ongoing: Review numbness, tingling and hearing changes regularly, especially after previous platinum/ototoxic medicines or age>65.
Response scans and examination follow the consultant plan, not a universal interval.
Routine cardiac echo, ECG series, DXA and genomic re-testing are not mandated by these two NCCP monotherapy protocols. Additional tests depend on symptoms, other medicines and clinical risks.

common_effects.name: Lower blood counts
common_effects.patient: Lower white cells raise infection risk; lower platelets can cause bruising or bleeding; anaemia can cause tiredness or breathlessness.
common_effects.frequency: Blood-count reductions are very common in the product information.

common_effects.name: Nausea, vomiting and tiredness
common_effects.patient: Anti-sickness treatment is prescribed to reduce nausea and vomiting. Plan rest and activity according to how you feel.
common_effects.frequency: Nausea, vomiting and weakness are very common in product information. Individual risk with modern prophylaxis differs.

common_effects.name: Bowel and mouth changes
common_effects.patient: Constipation, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort or mouth soreness may occur. Contact the team if you cannot drink or symptoms persist.

common_effects.name: Hair, taste and skin changes
common_effects.patient: Hair thinning or loss, altered taste and skin rashes may occur.

common_effects.name: Nerves, hearing and kidney effects
common_effects.patient: Report tingling, numbness, ringing in the ears, hearing change or passing much less urine. Blood tests and symptom review guide changes.

common_effects.name: Allergic reaction
common_effects.patient: Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, itching, rash, dizziness, chest discomfort, swelling or breathing difficulty during the infusion. Reactions can occur at the first treatment or after previous platinum courses.

common_effects.name: Uncommon serious and late harm
common_effects.patient: Serious infection, severe bleeding, organ injury and severe allergic reactions can occur. Very rarely, treatment-related blood disorders or other cancers are reported after chemotherapy. The consent discussion should cover the serious risks relevant to you.
common_effects.source: HPRA §4.4/4.8; avoid claiming precise regimen-specific percentages

urgent_actions: Contact the treatment unit urgently for fever, shaking chills, or feeling suddenly unwell, using the fever threshold and emergency number on your treatment card. Do not wait until the next appointment.

Get urgent advice for unusual bleeding, severe breathlessness, persistent vomiting or diarrhoea, inability to keep fluids down, markedly reduced urine, new confusion, seizures or sudden visual changes.

During infusion, tell staff immediately about breathing difficulty, swelling, chest pain, rash, dizziness or pain/burning around the cannula. Severe symptoms outside the unit need emergency assessment.
common.urgent_action_source: NCCP p5; HPRA §4.4/4.8. Local fever threshold/contact number must be inserted by the service, not invented.
self_care: Use your prescribed anti-sickness medicines and keep a record of persistent symptoms.
Drink regularly unless your team has given a fluid restriction. Ask before taking over-the-counter medicines, especially NSAIDs, or supplements.
Use gentle mouth care and ask for help with constipation, diarrhoea or mouth pain.
Follow your unit’s infection, food, vaccination and body-fluid precautions. Live vaccines need treatment-team advice.
Bring an updated medicine list, including anticoagulants, seizure medicines and supplements, to reviews.

fertility_pregnancy.patient: Discuss fertility preservation before treatment if relevant. Carboplatin may affect periods and fertility, sometimes permanently. Do not breastfeed during treatment. Discuss reliable contraception and contact the team immediately if pregnancy is possible.
fertility_pregnancy.verified_product_durations: The linked Irish SmPC advises effective contraception for women during treatment and at least6months afterwards; men should avoid fathering a child during treatment and at least3months afterwards. Confirm the actual product/local advice and any longer requirement from other medicines.

consent_points: Explain the goal of metastatic-breast treatment, expected uncertainty of benefit, alternatives and supportive care choices.
Document that breast use is off-label in Ireland, with consent and DTC/equivalent acknowledgement under local policy. Off-label does not by itself imply that a treatment is experimental.
Explain the difference between treatment days, recovery days and extra blood-test visits; the infusion itself is about30minutes, but the whole visit is longer.
Discuss blood-count/infection/bleeding risk, nausea, nerve/hearing effects, allergy, organ injury, fatigue, hair change and fertility.
Record the actual dose plan, review point and the patient’s priorities. Trial response percentages are group results, not an individual prediction.
logistics: Day-unit intravenous administration by trained staff; cannula or suitable existing vascular access according to local assessment.
NCCP administration is500mL glucose5% over30minutes. Unit preparation, antiemetics and observation add time.
Prescribed antiemetics are separate supportive medicines; no oral carboplatin tablets are taken at home.
No automatic port, continuous pump, home injection or mandatory overnight stay is implied by these source regimens.
Delays or dose changes may be needed after results or symptoms; never change the AUC yourself.

cautions: Do not insert indexed laboratory eGFR in mL/min/1.73m² as if it were mL/min.
Obesity, low muscle mass/low creatinine and postoperative changes can make estimates unreliable; measured GFR is preferred.
If no isotope value and overweight/obesity overstates GFR, adjusted ideal weight may be considered; it is not a mandatory default for all patients.
For creatinine<63µmol/L, considering62µmol/L or a steady preoperative result is discretionary; no silent flooring.

The current HPRA SmPC warns against Calvert after specified extensive pretreatment (mitomycinC, nitrosourea, doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide/cisplatin, combinations of≥5agents, or qualifying≥4500rad radiotherapy). Obtain specialist dose review.
The global generic calculator is not changed in this bounded proposal; the assessment never outputs a final milligram dose.

source_conflicts: NCCP protocols specify their own AUC4–6 schedules/counts. The linked product SmPC has broader labelled posology with different general count and interval recommendations. It supplements safety review and does not silently replace the exact NCCP thresholds.
HPRA allows possible individual benefit/risk exception below30mL/min; NCCP requires extreme caution at>20≤30 and excludes≤20. The proposal does not compute a dose in these bands.
NCCP says no routine hepatic adjustment; significant new/moderate-severe liver injury still requires review under current product safety warnings.

00251.title: Carboplatin alone every 4 weeks
00251.clinical_title: NCCP 00251 Carboplatin AUC4–6 Monotherapy–28 days v6
00251.course: Until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; the consultant individualises review points and treatment breaks.

timeline.text: Consent and medicine review; baseline blood count, kidney/liver tests and verified kidney-function measurement/estimate. Confirm your contact number and anti-sickness prescription.
Blood results and symptoms are reviewed, anti-sickness medicines are given, then carboplatin is infused over about30minutes. The total visit lasts longer.
Follow the prescribed anti-sickness plan and report uncontrolled symptoms.

timeline.when: Days 13–15 and Day 21 in the first cycles
timeline.text: Extra blood-count tests check how low the counts fall; these are monitoring visits, not extra carboplatin doses. Subsequent blood counts are taken before each cycle.
Recovery time, symptom monitoring and supportive care. There is no additional routine carboplatin dose during these days.
Repeat only after the treatment team confirms blood results, kidney dosing and tolerability. The schedule may change.

00251.count_rule: ANC>1 and platelets>100 for full dose; ANC<1 or platelets<100 delay. Exact1/100 unresolved and reviewed.
00251.other_source_indications: Nine gynaecology indication codes a–i retained.
00251.evidence_scope: TNT AUC6 every21days evidence is indirect for the q28 schedule; do not show trial outcome numbers as q28-specific.
hard_stops: Clinically severe marrow suppression or bleeding tumour
do_not_infer: No support because hypersensitivity premedication is usually unnecessary
